summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of neurogenic bladder, paraplegia, and recent pyelonephritis returned to the emergency department after eloping from the hospital less than 12 hours earlier. She presented with severe back pain, nausea, and tachycardia, which were attributed to cocaine use despite recent clinical improvement. She was treated with IV ceftriaxone and pain management, including a temporary groin central venous catheter for medication administration. Her condition stabilized, and she was transitioned to oral nitrofurantoin to complete her antibiotic course. Other medications were adjusted, including a reduced dose of amitriptyline and increased omeprazole. She was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to follow up and monitor for recurrent symptoms.
